answer: Propose latency-triangulated proof of place: each identity claims one physical location and, at random times, answers timing challenges from several independent beacons. A reply proves the claimant is near that spot, since light-speed limits stop one device faking many distant places at once. Like a relic found in one orchard, or a copper token stamped in one workshop, each identity occupies one place. An attacker running many fakes from one room fails triangulation; renting real devices worldwide costs a device and connection per identity, so Sybil cost scales linearly with no shortcut.
